name: Sprout Social
tagline: Publishing, engagement, listening, analytics, and customer care

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.limits: 5 social profiles, 1 seat priced separately, profile/post reporting and publishing workflow

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 5 social profiles, 10 brand keywords/group, consolidated inbox and review management

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Unlimited social profiles, 10 brand keywords/group, competitor/tag/paid insights

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: Unlimited social profiles, 20 brand keywords/group, API/helpdesk integrations and care reports

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom plan, onboarding, SSO setup and priority support

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 30-day free trial, no credit card; displayed annual rates require annual billing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every seat is billed separately; Premium Analytics, Listening, Employee Advocacy and professional services are separately priced add-ons; add-on prices are not public.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Sprout Social's durable value is platform APIs, distribution, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal enterprise social management planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: official platform OAuth credentials where available
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: direct publishing reliability as platform APIs change
protection from API and policy changes
whyPeopleStillPay: Sprout Social: Social tools survive because networks change APIs, permissions, formats, and anti-spam rules constantly.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, token refresh, media constraints, rate limits, scheduling, webhooks, retries, and platform policy compliance.

priorArt.name: Postiz

rejectedAlternatives.name: Postiz
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Scheduling, teams and analytics cover the commodity layer, not listening or enterprise care.

notes: Credibility row: Sprout Social survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Sprout Social; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build a personal enterprise social management planner that stores drafts, previews platform variants, and exports a posting queue without pretending to bypass platform APIs.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: direct publishing reliability as platform APIs change; reliable direct publishing across networks; analytics history and attribution.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
